test.name: Newspapers.com obituary search with date range
test.description: Newspapers.com has a different query structure from the record sites (keyword={first}+{last} with date-start/date-end and region/county parameters). The curated-links fixture returns only Ancestry URLs, so the Newspapers.com URL comes from the site-wide template. An obituary search needs the death window (1880-1905), not a single year.

input.delegation:
Search Newspapers.com for Patrick Flynn's obituary in Schuylkill County, between 1880 and 1905.

userPresent: yes
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Generated URL should target newspapers.com/search/results/ with the name as the query term and the 1880-1905 window and Pennsylvania/Schuylkill place expressed via its own date and place parameters (date-start/date-end and region/county, or equivalent) — not the record-site parameter style (no birthplace/birth= parameters)
Should provide capture-workflow instructions (click, save the results page or clipping as PDF, upload back) and note Newspapers.com is a paid site so a login may be required
A research-log entry must be written in the same turn the URL is generated: site newspapers, outcome partial, capture_received false, query capturing name + date range + place

The collections_search result for Schuylkill lists only a church-records collection and Pennsylvania probate records. A statement that FamilySearch's list for this place and period shows no newspaper collection, and so no FamilySearch copy to offer, is grounded in that result: the agent body asks for statements about which collections exist to rest on collections_search. It is not an unsupported claim and must not reduce Correctness.

Patrick's death is recorded in the project as March 1908, after the requested 1880-1905 window. Running the window the researcher asked for is correct (the agent body says to execute the chosen search, not override it), and pointing out the 1908 death and offering a wider search is a grounded observation, not a misleading one. Neither must reduce Correctness.
